description:
LANDED f986da97e on wt/kdt-close (PR #110, draft), 2026-09-03. Two of the
three original reader gaps were closed by measurement or by deletion during
scoping; this commit is the third plus the documents that had gone stale.

CLOSED WITHOUT CODE: gap (1), blind_escapes bailing on early.len() !=
late.len(), is PRESENT and REACHED but skips NOTHING -- an instrumented walk
at settled reads 87 pairs over 79 readable plans with ZERO length-guard skips,
because the plan-level skip already removes every plan whose arms could ask
different subject sets. Gap (2), separated_somewhere consulting only early's
subjects, is MOOT: that function was introduced by fz-kdt.178 and DELETED by
fz-kdt.186, replaced by seating, which enforces equal lengths.

THE CHANGE: the canon dump prints wrapper w{canonical} from ProgramCanon::
wrapper_order while PlanSite::Selection printed wrapper.identity, so a reader
following a wrapper number from a doc or a failure message into a dump landed
on the wrong wrapper. canon.rs now exposes canonical_wrapper_numbers (the
inverse of wrapper_order, #[cfg(test)] -- nothing in production labels a
wrapper for a dump reader); artifact_plans takes a &World; and
PlanSite::Selection carries { wrapper, canonical } and renders
`wrapper w{canonical} (published w{identity}) selection`. BOTH numbers,
because both have a reader: the canonical one leads to the dump, the published
one is what select_construction_member's runtime errors and a debugger show.
Rendering only the canonical number would have moved the trap rather than
closed it.

GATE: compiler2_a_selection_sites_label_names_the_wrapper_the_dump_prints
(0.6 s) checks that the dump heads one block per wrapper in canonical order,
asserts each label leads with the number heading its block, and ENDS by
asserting the two numberings disagree at all four sites so it cannot become a
tautology. Reverting Display to the identity form makes it fail with
`wrapper w0 selection` against canonical 2.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS TICKET'S OWN TEXT, both caught by measuring rather
than trusting it: (1) the gate subject named in the restated body,
enum_map_family, is IMPOSSIBLE -- it has ZERO PlanSite::Selection plans at
head, all twelve of its wrappers being single-member since fz-kdt.199, the
same collapse that blinded 00277. The gate is built on 00419_enum_take_mixed
(4 wrappers, 4 two-member selections, map 0->2, 1->3, 2->0, 3->1, no fixed
point), recorded in the gate's doc. (2) The 00277 canonical map in the body
was WRONG: it read w0->w4, w1->w2, w2->w3, w3->w0, w4->w1; measured it is
0->3, 1->4, 2->1, 3->2, 4->0. The committed doc carries the measured map.

STALE PROSE FIXED at all four named sites (dispatch-matrix.md, callsite_
dispatch.rs, and two in drive_test.rs), each now saying which numbering the
number was and that it names nothing at head -- 00277 has five wrappers, so
w13-w20 exist in neither numbering. dispatch-matrix.md's census table was
refreshed: call-edge 21, entry 169 with 162 unreadable, selection 49,
Region::List 103, 0 groups (it had said 17 / 153,146 / 86 / 87 / 44), and the
plan-order gate's comparand re-measured at 244 (it had said 261).

GATE: Coordinator gate on the folded branch (marker COORD-GATE-1788477267): fmt clean, zero build warnings, clippy clean, doctests clean, lib 1710 passed / 0 failed / 5 ignored in 86.6 s, fixture matrix single-threaded 509 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored.

comments.text: fz-kdt.179 landed (c3e27143d): member selection now runs the seat, but your two reader gaps are UNCHANGED and one is now the last census standing. INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_POPULATION (kept at 44 groups) still names CENSUS wrapper numbers, which differ from dump wN -- your dump-wN-vs-census-wN gap. And the static census reader's arm-pair skipping is retired for the SEAT census here but your description covers the reading logic that INDISTINGUISHABLE still uses. Re-measure against this base: the seat census is gone, so your scope narrows to INDISTINGUISHABLE's numbering and any reader the entry/case/receive censuses still use.

title: The static census reader skips arm pairs that ask different subject sets and consults separating subjects only on the earlier arm, where production covers walks the full position vector; and dump wrapper numbers differ from census wrapper numbers
